name: Japanese
about: Each hiragana stands for a whole syllable. Romanized with Hepburn.

phrases.how: Each sign is a syllable (こ ko, ん n, に ni, ち chi); the final は is read 'wa' here.
phrases.why: Greet someone in their own script on a card or a note.
phrases.dictation: Five hiragana. It ends with は, even though you say 'wa'.

phrases.how: が is か (ka) plus two small marks (dakuten) that turn it into 'ga'.
phrases.why: Write a real thank-you card to a host or to family.
phrases.dictation: Five hiragana: a-ri-ga-to-u. The long ō is written with う.

phrases.how: ず is す (su) with dakuten, which makes it 'zu'.
phrases.why: Spot it on a menu, a sign or a bottle label.
phrases.dictation: Two hiragana: み then ず.

phrases.how: だ is た (ta) plus dakuten = 'da'. Hiragana spells words by sound.
phrases.why: Sign a note to a friend. Writing it by hand helps you remember it.

phrases.how: Any word can be spelled in hiragana; いち is also written with the kanji 一.
phrases.why: Read quantities and order one of something off a menu.
phrases.dictation: Two hiragana: い then ち.
